title: Central Bank of India - 532885 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Central Bank of India Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR724 crore on a one-time INR632 crore DTA charge; FY26 net profit rose 15.43% to INR4,369 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 business grew 15.60% to INR812,439 crore, with gross advances up 18.76% to INR344,516 crore and deposits up 13.38% to INR467,923 crore. Q4 net profit fell to INR724 crore from INR1,034 crore a year earlier, mainly due to a one-time INR632 crore hit from recognising deferred tax assets at 25% instead of 35%. Q4 operating profit rose 4.64% YoY to INR2,096 crore, but fell QoQ as treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore) and recoveries from written-off accounts (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore) dropped. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis: gross NPA 2.67% (down 51 bps YoY), net NPA 0.49%, slippage ratio 1.16% vs 1.45%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,034 crore Q4 FY25 (after INR632 crore one-time DTA charge)
marginal decline; Q4 about 2.9% excluding INR431 crore tax refund interest
GNPA -51 bps YoY; NNPA +6 bps per call (analyst noted rise)

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances INR103,533 crore, up 25.67% YoY; management called retail, agriculture and MSME (RAM) the main growth engine.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances INR61,687 crore, up 17.60% YoY.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances INR69,351 crore, up 17.06% YoY; Q4 slippages partly linked to MSME branch audits and MUDRA/PMEGP accounts up to INR10 lakh.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book INR109,945 crore, up 14.50% YoY; bank is selective, targeting good-rated borrowers only. RAM/corporate split is 58:32 per call, with a 65:35 +/-5 target.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book around INR28,000 crore, growth 8.6%; LTV and yield not disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: business growth 14% to 15%, deposit growth 10% to 12%, advances growth 14% to 16%.
NIM to be maintained above 3%, supported by deposit repricing expected to complete next quarter.

ECL migration effective 1 April 2027; INR1,525 crore already provided. Management says it can absorb full day-one impact through reserves at 17.91% CRAR. Ongoing ECL-related provisions estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore of tax-rate benefit (25% vs 35%).
FY27 capex budget INR1,442 crore and revenue budget INR1,276 crore for digital spend.
Expects to recover INR2,200 crore to INR2,500 crore from technically written-off accounts in FY27 (INR2,270 crore recovered in FY26 from over INR32,000 crore pool). Dividend to be maintained.
capex_capacity: FY27 capital budget for digital spend INR1,442 crore; revenue budget INR1,276 crore.
Sales and marketing team being set up, 50% through IBPS recruitment, expected within 1 to 2 months.
Around 900 officers from training to be deployed in October; 1,000 credit officers being trained.
Outreach programme held in more than 100 locations since November; 225 MSME and more than 300 agriculture branches identified for focus.
Wealth management division, credit card business and centralised forex set up or being established.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances 7.78% in Q4 vs 8.21% a year earlier (down 57 bps); cost of deposits 4.82% (down 2 bps). About 61% of advances are external-benchmark linked, so repricing hit yields faster than deposits.
CD ratio 73.80% in March 2026 (66% in September 2025), roughly 74%; LCR 210% in FY26.
Term deposit growth above 14% to 15%; saving bank deposits crossed INR2 lakh crore for the first time, growing 10.05%.
Government business cell MoUs with state governments, railways and police/paramilitary forces are driving salary accounts.
No stress signals from the Middle East situation so far; no requests for overdue PCs or post-shipment facilities. Daily slippage of about INR250 crore recorded around 20 April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating profit and net profit fall QoQ, and is there stress from geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore in Q3) and lower written-off recoveries (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore). Net profit was hit by the INR632 crore DTA charge. No stress signals have appeared so far from the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fresh slippages rise QoQ to INR1,301 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukul Dandige attributed part of the rise to MSME accounts flagged in branch audits where credit submissions did not match business projections, and to some agriculture accounts. Government-scheme (MUDRA, PMEGP) accounts up to INR10 lakh also slipped; the normal run-rate is about INR800 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on the one-time charge and recurring credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's back-of-envelope estimate of the ECL impact is around INR4,000 crore, of which INR1,525 crore is already provided. Ongoing ECL-related provisions are estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by a tax benefit of roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore. The full simulation is not complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise about 30 bps QoQ when yields and funding costs were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Dandige said a INR431 crore income-tax interest refund booked in Q4 added to NIM. Excluding it, NIM was about 2.89% to 2.9% in Q4 vs 2.96% in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are standard asset provisions and gold loan details?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard asset provisions are about 0.7% to 0.8% of standard assets, around INR2,800 crore to INR2,900 crore in total, including the INR1,525 crore ECL provision and RBI restructuring provisions. Gold loans are about INR28,000 crore, growing 8.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for NIM and recovery from written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM will stay above 3% in FY27 given CASA strength and RAM mix. It expects INR2,200 crore to INR2,500 crore of recoveries from written-off accounts in FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 one-time DTA charge of INR632 crore; the tax refund (INR431 crore) inflated Q4 NIM and profit, so underlying quarterly profit is lower than reported.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027: the simulation is not finished and no final impact number has been given.
Q4 slippage rose to INR1,301 crore vs about INR800 crore average; FY27 slippage target is below 1%.
Yield pressure from external-benchmark-linked loans (about 61%) versus slower deposit repricing; NIM guidance of above 3% depends on repricing finishing next quarter.
Treasury income dropped to INR9 crore in Q4; the lumpy airline account recovery process is ongoing (INR515 crore guarantee received previously).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, capital and asset quality, but evasive on specifics: ECL impact, the pipeline, and offline-only items (technology, sanctions) were deferred. Management framed the Q4 profit fall as largely one-time and downplayed the slippage increase.
key_quotes: And here, I want to mention as per the New Finance Bill, bank has taken a onetime impact of INR632 crores due to recognition of deferred tax asset at the rate of 25% as against 35%.
So bank being sufficiently capitalized at 17.91%, I can easily take the impact on day 1.
We have given direction that we are going to remain above 3%.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 14-15% business growth, 14-16% advances growth and 10-12% deposit growth; backing cited is RAM growth momentum, a sales team being set up, and new wealth, card and forex businesses, with no specific capacity, orders or contracts given with numbers.
